page: Microsoft Azure D32als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Dalsv7 server family. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz, this instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system features an x86_64 architecture and is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is designated as Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing placing the instance in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded decompression via bzip3 also registers in the top 10%, while gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression show strong performance in the top 25% tier. Overall multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and PassMark CPU testing falls into the average and strong categories respectively. Memory bandwidth tests for both read and write operations consistently place in the middle 50% average tier. For specialized workloads, the CPU's support for AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions contributes to strong performance in small-model LLM inference tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32als_v7 offers a streamlined hardware profile by pairing high-frequency compute cores with a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio. This design minimizes memory overhead costs for workloads that are primarily CPU-bound rather than memory-intensive. The absence of local storage and integrated GPUs further refines the cost structure, making it a targeted choice for specific processing tasks. This instance is highly suited for compute-heavy workloads such as web serving, batch processing, single-threaded data decompression, and lightweight machine learning inference.
